## Context
Independent review of ticket 5f4d found two non-blocking hardening gaps in
scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py. A file containing invalid UTF-8 is skipped wholesale
(`except UnicodeDecodeError: continue`), so a source file can evade the guard by carrying one
bad byte. Separately, an unallowlisted match prints the complete raw source line, so a very
long line or embedded control characters land unescaped in CI logs.

## Plan
- Define a source-ish text extension set (`.py`, `.md`, `.json`, `.yaml`/`.yml`, `.toml`) that
  must FAIL CLOSED on a decode error, while every other extension stays tolerated so genuine
  binaries do not produce false positives.
- Bound and escape diagnostic excerpts: escape non-printable characters and cap the escaped excerpt at
  200 characters (`MAX_EXCERPT_CHARS = 200`), with an explicit truncation marker.
- Add behavioral tests for invalid-byte source input, invalid-byte binary input, and
  hostile (long / control-character) matching lines.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py -q` — new cases: an
  undecodable `.py` exits 1 naming the file, an undecodable `.bin` exits 0, and a long
  control-character line is emitted escaped and truncated.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — the guard is itself part of the `make lint` gate, so a
  clean run proves the real repository still scans clean.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Known text files cannot evade the vocabulary guard by containing an invalid UTF-8 byte:
      verified by a test asserting exit 1 and the offending path in stderr.
- [x] Binary files remain safely ignored without false positives: verified by a test asserting
      exit 0 for an undecodable non-source extension.
- [x] Diagnostics escape control characters and cap source excerpts at 200 characters: verified by a test asserting no raw control byte and a truncation marker in stderr.
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py -q` and `make lint` pass.
